# zhpgvx

> Computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a complex Hermitian-definite generalized eigenproblem in packed storage.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zhpgvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zhpgvx';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zhpgvx(
    order,
    itype,
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N,
    AP,
    BP,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW,
    Z, LDZ,
    WORK,
    RWORK,
    IWORK,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL
) → integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `itype` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `itype < 1 \|\| itype > 3` | problem type (1, 2, or 3) |
| `jobz` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `range` | `("all"\|"value"\|"index")` | in |  | one of `'all'`, `'index'`, `'value'` | `'all'`, `'value'`, or `'index'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of matrices A and B |
| `AP` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | packed Hermitian matrix A (length N*(N+1)/2) |
| `BP` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | packed Hermitian positive definite matrix B (length N*(N+1)/2) |
| `vl` | `number` | in |  |  | lower bound of eigenvalue interval (range='value') |
| `vu` | `number` | in |  | rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` | upper bound of eigenvalue interval (range='value') |
| `il` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && il < 1` | index of smallest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, range='index') |
| `iu` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N)` | index of largest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, range='index') |
| `abstol` | `number` | in |  |  | absolute tolerance for eigenvalues |
| `m` | `Int32Array` | out |  |  | output (length-1 array): the total number of eigenvalues found |
| `w` | `Float64Array` | out | `N` |  | output array for eigenvalues (length N) |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `w` |
| `Z` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)` |  | output eigenvector matrix (N x M) |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | rejects `ldz < 1 \|\| (jobz === 'compute-vectors' && ldz < N)` | leading dimension of Z (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `(Complex128Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | complex workspace (length >= 2*N) |
| `RWORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 7 * N` |  | real workspace (length >= 7*N) |
| `IWORK` | `(Int32Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 5 * N` |  | integer workspace (length >= 5*N) |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array` | out | `N` |  | output: indices of non-converged eigenvectors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `IFAIL` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `itype`: Specifies the problem type to be solved:

  -   `= 1`: $A \, x = (\lambda ) \, B \, x$
  -   `= 2`: $A \, B \, x = (\lambda ) \, x$
  -   `= 3`: $B \, A \, x = (\lambda ) \, x$
- `jobz`:

  -   `= 'N'`: Compute eigenvalues only;
  -   `= 'V'`: Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
- `range`:

  -   `= 'A'`: all eigenvalues will be found;
  -   `= 'V'`: all eigenvalues in the half-open interval (`VL`,`VU`\] will be found;
  -   `= 'I'`: the `IL`-th through `IU`-th eigenvalues will be found.
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangles of A and B are stored;
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangles of A and B are stored.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.
- `AP`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2*n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.

  On exit, the contents of `AP` are destroyed.
- `BP`: On entry, the upper or lower triangle of the Hermitian matrix B, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of B is stored in the array `BP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `BP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = B(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `BP(i + (j-1)*(2*n-j)/2) = B(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$.

  On exit, the triangular factor U or L from the Cholesky factorization $B = U^H \, U$ or $B = L \, L^H$, in the same storage format as B.
- `vl`: If `RANGE='V'`, the lower bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `vu`: If `RANGE='V'`, the upper bound of the interval to be searched for eigenvalues. $\mathrm{VL} < \mathrm{VU}$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'I'.
- `il`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the smallest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `iu`: If `RANGE='I'`, the index of the largest eigenvalue to be returned. $1 \le \mathrm{IL} \le \mathrm{IU} \le N$, if $N > 0$; `IL = 1` and `IU = 0` if $N = 0$. Not referenced if `RANGE = 'A'` or 'V'.
- `abstol`: The absolute error tolerance for the eigenvalues. An approximate eigenvalue is accepted as converged when it is determined to lie in an interval \[a,b\] of width less than or equal to

  $$
  \mathrm{ABSTOL} + \mathrm{EPS} \, \max ( |a|,|b| )
  $$

  where EPS is the machine precision. If `ABSTOL` is less than or equal to zero, then EPS\*\|T\| will be used in its place, where \|T\| is the 1-norm of the tridiagonal matrix obtained by reducing `AP` to tridiagonal form.

  Eigenvalues will be computed most accurately when `ABSTOL` is set to twice the underflow threshold $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$, not zero. If this routine returns with $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, indicating that some eigenvectors did not converge, try setting `ABSTOL` to $2 \, \mathrm{DLAMCH}(\text{'S'})$.
- `m`: The total number of eigenvalues found. $0 \le M \le N$. If `RANGE = 'A'`, $M = N$, and if `RANGE = 'I'`, $M = \mathrm{IU}-\mathrm{IL}+1$.
- `w`: On normal exit, the first M elements contain the selected eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `Z`: If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then Z is not referenced. If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M columns of Z contain the orthonormal eigenvectors of the matrix A corresponding to the selected eigenvalues, with the i-th column of Z holding the eigenvector associated with `W(i)`. The eigenvectors are normalized as follows: if `ITYPE = 1` or 2, $Z^H \, B \, Z = I$; if `ITYPE = 3`, $Z^H \, \operatorname{inv}(B) \, Z = I$.

  If an eigenvector fails to converge, then that column of Z contains the latest approximation to the eigenvector, and the index of the eigenvector is returned in `IFAIL`. Note: the user must ensure that at least max(1,M) columns are supplied in the array Z; if `RANGE = 'V'`, the exact value of M is not known in advance and an upper bound must be used.
- `IFAIL`: If `JOBZ = 'V'`, then if `INFO = 0`, the first M elements of `IFAIL` are zero. If $\mathrm{INFO} > 0$, then `IFAIL` contains the indices of the eigenvectors that failed to converge. If `JOBZ = 'N'`, then `IFAIL` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument is invalid (rejected when `itype < 1 \|\| itype > 3`)
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` fifth argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && il < 1`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < N )`)
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDZ < 1 \|\| ( jobz === "compute-vectors" && LDZ < max( 1, range === "index" ? iu - il + 1 : N ) )`)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zhpgvx.ndarray(
    itype,
    jobz, range, uplo,
    N,
    AP, strideAP, offsetAP,
    BP, strideBP, offsetBP,
    vl, vu, il, iu, abstol,
    m,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork,
    IFAIL, strideIFAIL, offsetIFAIL
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `itype` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `itype < 1 \|\| itype > 3` | problem type (1, 2, or 3) |
| `jobz` | `("no-vectors"\|"compute-vectors")` | in |  | one of `'no-vectors'`, `'compute-vectors'` | `'no-vectors'` or `'compute-vectors'` |
| `range` | `("all"\|"value"\|"index")` | in |  | one of `'all'`, `'index'`, `'value'` | `'all'`, `'value'`, or `'index'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | in |  | one of `'lower'`, `'upper'` | `'upper'` or `'lower'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of matrices A and B |
| `AP` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | packed Hermitian matrix A; on exit, overwritten |
| ↳ `strideAP` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `AP` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetAP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `AP` (complex elements) |
| `BP` | `Complex128Array` | in/out | `trunc( N * (N + 1) / 2 )` |  | packed Hermitian positive definite matrix B; on exit, Cholesky factor |
| ↳ `strideBP` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `BP` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetBP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `BP` (complex elements) |
| `vl` | `number` | in |  |  | lower bound of eigenvalue interval (range='value') |
| `vu` | `number` | in |  | rejects `range === 'value' && (N > 0 && vu <= vl)` | upper bound of eigenvalue interval (range='value') |
| `il` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && il < 1` | index of smallest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, range='index') |
| `iu` | `integer` | in |  | rejects `range !== 'value' && range === 'index' && (iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N)` | index of largest eigenvalue to compute (1-based, range='index') |

| `Z` | `Complex128Array` | out | `N × (range === 'index' ? iu - il + 1 : N)` |  | output eigenvector matrix (N x M) |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `Z` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `Z` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `Z` (complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array` | out | `≥ 2 * N` |  | complex workspace array (length >= 2*N) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `WORK` (complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `WORK` (complex elements) |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ 7 * N` |  | real workspace array (length >= 7*N) |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `RWORK` |

| `IWORK` | `Int32Array` | out | `≥ 5 * N` |  | integer workspace (length >= 5*N) |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `IWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `IWORK` |
| `IFAIL` | `Int32Array` | out | `N` |  | output: indices of non-converged eigenvectors (length N) |
| ↳ `strideIFAIL` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `IFAIL` |

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument is invalid (rejected when `itype < 1 \|\| itype > 3`)
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "index", "value"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range === "value" && ( N > 0 && vu <= vl )`)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && il < 1`)
- `RangeError` fifteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `range !== "value" && range === "index" && ( iu < min( N, il ) \|\| iu > N )`)
- `RangeError` `RWORK` must have at least `7 * N` elements from `offsetRWork`
- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `5 * N` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: ZPPTRF or ZHPEVX returned an error code: \<= N:  if `INFO = i`, ZHPEVX failed to converge; i eigenvectors failed to converge.  Their indices are stored in array `IFAIL`.
-   `> N`: if $\mathrm{INFO} = N + i$, for $1 \le i \le n$, then the leading principal minor of order i of B is not positive. The factorization of B could not be completed and no eigenvalues or eigenvectors were computed.

## Notes

-   `zhpgvx()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZHPGVX`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zhpgvx.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import zhpgvx from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zhpgvx';

// A = [4 1-i; 1+i 5] in upper packed storage (complex interleaved):
const m = new Int32Array( 1 );

const AP = new Complex128Array( [ 4, 0, 1, -1, 5, 0 ] );

// B = [2 0; 0 3] in upper packed storage:
const BP = new Complex128Array( [ 2, 0, 0, 0, 3, 0 ] );

const W = new Float64Array( 2 );
const Z = new Complex128Array( 4 );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( 10 );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( 20 );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( 15 );
const IFAIL = new Int32Array( 2 );

const info = zhpgvx( 'column-major', 1, 'compute-vectors', 'all', 'upper', 2, AP, BP, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, m, W, 1, Z, 2, WORK, RWORK, IWORK, IFAIL, 1 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'M (eigenvalues found):', m[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'Eigenvalues (W):', W ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'Eigenvectors (Z):', Z ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZHPGVX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZHPGVX computes selected eigenvalues and, optionally, eigenvectors of a complex generalized Hermitian-definite eigenproblem, of the form $A \, x=(\lambda ) \, B \, x$, $A \, \mathrm{Bx}=(\lambda ) \, x$, or $B \, A \, x=(\lambda ) \, x$. Here A and B are assumed to be Hermitian, stored in packed format, and B is also positive definite. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors can be selected by specifying either a range of values or a range of indices for the desired eigenvalues.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
